question: Does the supreme scripture posit a separate substrate for the powers as qualities?
premises: In the scripture of the Supreme Lord, no substrate for the powers is taught.
The powers are not treated as qualities needing an external support.
This differs from the Kanāda school's doctrine of an unseen quality.
inference: Therefore the powers are not dependent on any separate substrate in the manner of qualities.
uncertainties: The precise target of 'kāṇādadṛṣṭivat' may be the Vaiśeṣika notion of adṛṣṭa or more generally their quality-substrate model.
plain_english: In the scripture of the Supreme Lord, the powers are not said to have any separate substrate, as if they were qualities in the manner taught by the followers of Kaṇāda.
